title: You say “Lord”… but you still make the final call.
paragraphs: You say “Lord”… but you still make the final call.
You pray—but only after you’ve already decided what you’re going to do.
You sing “I surrender all”—but there are parts of your life you’ve quietly labeled untouchable.
And you don’t even flinch anymore when conviction knocks.
Because you’ve learned how to call Jesus “Lord”… without actually giving Him control.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

That’s not a small inconsistency.
That’s a contradiction that Scripture confronts directly.
Jesus said it plainly:
“Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I tell you?” (Luke 6:46)
Read that again.

He didn’t question their words.
He questioned their obedience.

Because in the world Jesus stepped into, “Lord” wasn’t a casual title.
It meant authority. Ownership. Absolute right to command.
To call someone “Lord” and still live as your own authority…
…was unthinkable.
But you’ve made it normal.

You say He’s Lord over your life—
but your decisions still run through your feelings, your plans, your timing.
God saw it.

That moment you knew what Scripture said…
…and chose differently anyway.
You knew.
And you justified it.

You called it wisdom.
You called it “waiting for peace.”
You called it “being realistic.”
But underneath it all…
You stayed in control.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because Scripture doesn’t leave room for a divided throne.
“No one can serve two masters…” (Matthew 6:24)

Not God and your will.
Not Jesus and your autonomy.
One will rule.
The other will be reduced to a voice you occasionally consult.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
This is where many people deceive themselves.

They believe they’ve surrendered…
when what they’ve actually done is delegated certain areas to God while keeping ultimate authority.

They let Him guide their words—but not their relationships.
They trust Him with Sunday—but not their future.
They obey when it’s easy—but hesitate when it costs them.
That’s not Lordship.
That’s negotiation.
And Jesus never negotiated His place.
“Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.” (Luke 9:23)
Deny yourself.

Not improve yourself.
Not partially adjust.
Deny.

That means your preferences don’t lead.
Your desires don’t rule.
Your life is no longer yours.
That’s where everything shifts.
Because now the real question surfaces:

Do you want a Savior…
or a Lord?
Because you cannot separate them.

Romans 10:9 says,
“If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.”
Not just believe.
Confess Him as Lord.
Authority. Rule. Reign.
That means surrender isn’t a one-time emotional moment.
It’s a daily death.

A daily choice to step off the throne of your own life…
and let Jesus take the seat you’ve been guarding.
And yes—it will feel like loss at first.
Because control feels safe.
It gives the illusion that you’re protecting yourself.
But control is also what’s been keeping you trapped.

Your anxiety.
Your constant second-guessing.
Your exhaustion from trying to manage everything.
That’s the fruit of a life where you are lord.
But Jesus offers something radically different.
“Come to me, all who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.” (Matthew 11:28)
Rest doesn’t come from better control.
It comes from surrendering it.
From trusting that His will is not just higher—but better.

Even when it cuts.
Even when it redirects everything you planned.
Because at the center of this is the Gospel itself.
You were never meant to save yourself.
Your sin proved that.
Your failures confirmed it.

You couldn’t carry the weight of your own righteousness…
so Jesus carried the cross instead.

He lived the life you couldn’t.
Died the death you deserved.
Rose again to offer you something you could never earn.
Grace.
But grace doesn’t leave you in control.
Grace transfers ownership.
“You are not your own, for you were bought with a price…” (1 Corinthians 6:19–20)
Bought.
That means your life now belongs to Him.

Not partially.
Not seasonally.
Fully.

So no—
it is not possible to truly call Jesus “Lord” and remain in control of your life.
One of those will always give way to the other.
And right now…
You already know which one has been winning.
But this is the moment where that can change.

Not by trying harder.
Not by managing your behavior better.
But by finally surrendering what you’ve been protecting.
Your will.
Your control.
Your right to decide everything on your own.
That’s where real freedom begins.

If something in you is resisting this…
say it.

If something in you knows this is true…
don’t ignore it.
Write it out. Admit it.
Because silence is where compromise survives.

And someone you know is living in the same tension—
share this with them. Let it confront them too.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—where your faith is sharpened, corrected, and anchored in Scripture in a way that doesn’t let you stay comfortable—

Because the difference between calling Him “Lord”…
and actually living under His Lordship…
is the difference between illusion and transformation.
